rationale:
Evidence: the raced iteration 2 design (score 132.0028) is the best so far. Its outcome row is kp 2.8, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, with sensors at x -0.06 to +0.06, y 0.06, 16 mm footprints. It is the only design with a finish (oval, 1.88 s) and has the highest progress on every track (oval 0.45, s-bend 0.27, slalom 0.16). Iteration 3 (ki 0.6) scored lower at 122.2, so ki stays at 0.3.

Record discrepancy: the entity1 text and the round-2 critique cite kp 3.0 for iteration 2. The outcome table and the iteration 2 produced entity both show kp 2.8, and the score is tied to the raced design. I use kp 2.8 so that this race differs from the 132.0 baseline in base_speed alone.

What I accepted from the round-2 critique: (1) The test is cleanly isolated. Relative to the raced baseline, only base_speed changes, from 1.6 to 1.8. (2) The max_error trigger cannot discriminate, because off-track runs end at the 0.06 m limit. I therefore do not use max_error to decide the next step. I use progress, off-track ends, and line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom. (3) The success criterion is stated explicitly below. (4) Speed matters for progress and completion more than for the time term, which is at most about 22 points on the oval.

What I rejected: (a) Reverting to 1.6 now, which would not add information. (b) Changing kp to 3.0 in the same race, which would confound the speed test. (c) Changing sensor span or footprint this round. Iteration 1 showed a span change did not move max_error, so I keep geometry fixed until the speed effect is known. (d) Lowering speed for the time bonus, since completion is worth 500 points.

What I changed: base_speed 1.6 to 1.8. Everything else matches the raced iteration 2 design.

Success criterion: the test passes only if the score exceeds 132.0 and off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom do not rise. A gain on the oval alone does not count if progress falls on the s-bend or slalom.

Expected result (a guess, not a measurement): progress equal to or above the baseline on the oval, with a faster oval finish possible. Lateral load rises with speed on the bends, so progress on the s-bend and slalom could fall. I give this roughly even odds.

Decision rule for the next round: if the score exceeds 132.0 with s-bend and slalom progress and off-track ends no worse, keep 1.8 and test whether line_loss_events on the s-bend (0.65) and slalom (0.8) fall. If the score falls or off-track ends rise, return to 1.6 and test a sensor footprint change on the s-bend and slalom. If progress is flat at 1.8, the steady-bias explanation is next, tested as a smaller ki (about 0.1) on its own.
